summary: Owned units s0001–s0022 of Jinshu 80 were read in Chinese against every owned claim, hint, and person. The chapter gives one explicit age (年十三) and no birth years; those were correctly left unconverted. One-sided termini that rest on another person's death in the Jin annals are sound: Zhou Yi was killed in Yongchang 1 (AD 322), Wang Dun died in Taining 2 (AD 324), so the ox-heart visit and Dun’s praise of Xizhi are on or before those years. 元帝之過江 maps to Huai-di Yongjia 1 / AD 307 (Jinshu Yuan-di ji says 永嘉初; Tongjian dates the arrival at Jianye to month 9). Yu Liang’s western command and 亮臨薨 convert to AD 334–340 and AD 340 from Cheng-di Xianhe 9 and Xiankang 6 I/庚子, a January date that remains AD 340 in both Julian and proleptic Gregorian. The unsupported conversion is 時太尉郗鑒 → a closed AD 338–339 marriage window. Xi Jian did hold 太尉 from Xiankang 4 V to Xiankang 5 VIII, but the same anecdote in Shishuo Xin yu calls him 郗太傅, this chapter already uses 司徒導 as a later label, and published reconstructions place the match in Taining 1–2. That interval invents a start year and chooses one reading. No births were omitted from these units; Yu Liang’s death is the only death the Chinese states.

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi is stated to have been thirteen sui when he called on Zhou Yi.
itemChecks.reason: s0007 says 年十三 of Wang Xizhi, the owner of this age claim. The row keeps reckoning sui and does not invent a birth year from inclusive age. No competing age figure appears in the owned units.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang, near death, submitted a memorial and died in Cheng-di Xiankang 6.
itemChecks.reason: s0020’s 亮臨薨 is Yu Liang’s own dying act, not a descendant commemoration. Jinshu Cheng-di ji dates the death to 咸康六年春正月庚子, the conventional Western year AD 340. The claim uses year precision rather than a day, so no Julian/Gregorian New Year shift arises; Xiankang 6 I remains AD 340 under both conventions.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi at thirteen sui visited Zhou Yi and was first served the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The visit is Xizhi’s own event (年十三，嘗謁周顗; 顗先割啖羲之). Zhou Yi was killed in Yuan-di Yongchang 1 (annals: 周顗爲敦所害), so the living reception cannot postdate AD 322. onOrBefore 322 is a genuine one-sided bound; no start year was invented, and 年十三 was not turned into a birth year.

evidence.quote: 年十三，嘗謁周顗，顗察而異之
顗先割啖羲之，於是始知名

itemChecks.event: As a boy Wang Xizhi was slow of speech and not thought remarkable.
itemChecks.reason: s0006 describes childhood speech, with no reign year or era. undatedSourceAttestation is required; a guessed Western year would be improper.

evidence.quote: 羲之幼訥於言，人未之奇

itemChecks.event: In adulthood Wang Xizhi was eloquent, famed for integrity, and preeminent in clerical script.
itemChecks.reason: s0009’s 及長 is a life-stage note, not a calendar date. Leaving the attestation undated matches the Chinese.

evidence.quote: 及長，辯贍，以骨鯁稱，尤善隸書

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi was commended for integrity and judgment in Yu Liang’s deathbed memorial.
itemChecks.reason: The dated event belongs to Xizhi as the living subject of 上疏稱羲之, timed by Yu Liang’s 臨薨, not as later reception. Cheng-di Xiankang 6 I/庚子 is AD 340 at year precision. This is contemporaneous praise while Xizhi was serving, not a retrospective honor.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Dao is identified as Minister of Education only in Wang Xizhi’s kinship line.
itemChecks.reason: 司徒導之從子也 is a later office-label in a genealogy, not a dated act of Dao’s. The same chapter’s use of a highest title here shows why 司徒 must stay undated—and why 太尉 in s0014 cannot be treated as a safer date marker than this 司徒.

itemChecks.event: Wang Zheng is attested as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing with no reign year.
itemChecks.reason: s0003 names 祖正，尚書郎 and nothing else. Owner is Wang Zheng; no Western year is licensed.

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang first proposed the plan when the future Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi.
itemChecks.reason: 曠首創其議 is Kuang’s own counsel, dated by 元帝之過江也. Yuan-di ji says 永嘉初，用王導計，始鎮建鄴; Tongjian places the arrival at Jianye in Yongjia 1 month 9 (戊申), still the conventional Western year AD 307. The chapter gives no month, so year precision is right. This is the 307 southward transfer, not the 311 Yongjia refugee wave.

evidence.quote: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang is named Administrator of Huainan in the genealogy without a reign year.
itemChecks.reason: 父曠，淮南太守 is an undated career label. It must not borrow AD 307 from the following crossing sentence.

itemChecks.event: The future Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi and established himself at Jianye.
itemChecks.reason: 元帝之過江也 names Yuan’s own crossing; the later title 元帝 is how the biography refers to Sima Rui and does not turn this into reception. Yongjia 1 / AD 307 is the chronicle year for 始鎮建鄴. He was not yet emperor; the event dated is the crossing, not the 317 accession.

itemChecks.event: Zhou Yi received the thirteen-sui Wang Xizhi and first offered him the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: The reception is Zhou Yi’s own act (顗察而異之; 顗先割啖羲之). He was killed in Yongchang 1, so onOrBefore AD 322 is the secure terminus. The source date 年十三 is Xizhi’s age, used only as the occasion, not converted into Zhou Yi’s lifespan.

itemChecks.event: Wang Dun as paternal uncle esteemed Wang Xizhi and compared him with Clerk Ruan.
itemChecks.reason: 敦嘗謂羲之曰 is Dun’s own speech. Ming-di Taining 2 VII records 王敦憤惋而死, so the conversation is on or before AD 324. sourceDate 從伯敦 is only the kinship cue; the bound is the death terminus, not an invented exact year.

evidence.quote: 敦嘗謂羲之曰：「汝是吾家佳子弟，當不減阮主簿。」

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu served as Wang Dun’s chief clerk and was named by Dun as the standard for Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: 為敦主簿 and Dun’s 不減阮主簿 compare Ruan with Xizhi while Dun lived. The same Taining 2 death gives onOrBefore AD 324. Ruan’s later 王氏三少 remark is not given its own year here.

evidence.quote: 時陳留阮裕有重名，為敦主簿

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu grouped Wang Cheng with Xizhi and Wang Yue as the three young men of the Wang clan.
itemChecks.reason: 王承 appears only in this undated appraisal. No reign year is present; undatedSourceAttestation is correct. 三少 is not a twin inference.

evidence.quote: 裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu grouped Wang Yue with Xizhi and Wang Cheng as the three young men of the Wang clan.
itemChecks.reason: 王悅 is named in the same undated sentence as Cheng. No calendar conversion is possible from s0013 alone.

evidence.quote: 羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian sent a student to Wang Dao to seek a son-in-law among the Wang youths.
itemChecks.reason: The event is Xi Jian’s own matchmaking (時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導). Cheng-di Xiankang 4 V made him 太尉 and Xiankang 5 VIII he died, so AD 338–339 is his actual tenure—but that does not license a closed event window. This chapter already uses 司徒導 as a non-dating label; Shishuo Xin yu tells the same story as 郗太傅在京口, a title Xi Jian never held; Wang Dao and Xi Jian were both alive until AD 339, which supports only onOrBefore 339. Published reconstructions read 時 as Taining 1–2. The row invents a 338 start and treats one title-reading as settled.

evidence.quote: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導
訪之，乃羲之也，遂以女妻之

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian’s daughter was given in marriage to Wang Xizhi after the east-bed inspection.
itemChecks.reason: 遂以女妻之 is the daughter’s own marriage, owned by p012. It inherits the same 338–339 interval from 時太尉. The Chinese gives no era year. The secure shared terminus is that Xi Jian and Wang Dao were alive (both dead in Xiankang 5 / AD 339). A 338 start assumes 太尉 is contemporaneous and discards the 太傅 anecdote and the Taining reading. That is false precision, not a justified uncertainty window.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang, as General Who Conquers the West, recruited Wang Xizhi as an army adviser.
itemChecks.reason: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍 is Yu Liang’s own recruitment under that military title, not a dynasty-long activity span. After Tao Kan’s death in Xianhe 9 the annals give Liang the six-province command (still styled 平西 in that line; the bio and later annals use 征西). He is still 征西將軍 in Xiankang 4 and dies in Xiankang 6. AD 334–340 is uncertainty about when the 參軍 appointment fell inside that command, not an invented exact year.

evidence.quote: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，累遷長史

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang on the point of death memorialized the throne in praise of Wang Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: Same 亮臨薨 act as claim-115, owned by Yu Liang. Xiankang 6 I/庚子 supports westernYear AD 340 at year precision. Not a reception date and not Xizhi’s life-span endpoint.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Xizhi was commended in Yu Liang’s deathbed memorial and later wrote during the Yin Hao–Huan Wen conflict.
itemChecks.reason: AD 340 matches Xizhi’s own commending at 亮臨薨 (claim-152). AD 351–353 matches the supplied context item on 時殷浩與桓溫不協 and the Kuaiji letters, Xizhi’s own counsel, not a posthumous honor. The childhood visit’s onOrBefore 322 is a personal event but not official activity; omitting it from active hints does not import a later reception into life dates. No death date from later in the chapter is used.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

itemChecks.event: Wang Dao, recalled as Chancellor Wang, once tried to bring Wang Xizhi into office.
itemChecks.reason: The owned kinship label 司徒導 is undated. The hint AD 317–339 copies the supplied context row for 王丞相時, a single remembered recruitment whose window is the conventional span from the 317 restoration to Dao’s Xiankang 5 death, not a claim that he was active every year of a dynasty. Strict 丞相 tenure is only Xiankang 4–5; that narrower reading lives on the context item, which this job does not re-judge.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint is correct because Wang Zheng has no dated personal event in these units.
itemChecks.reason: s0003 only titles him 尚書郎. An empty active-hint array matches the absence of a calendar event.

itemChecks.event: Wang Kuang first proposed the plan for Emperor Yuan’s crossing of the Yangzi.
itemChecks.reason: AD 307 is Kuang’s own 首創其議, tied to 元帝之過江 and Yongjia 1. The undated 淮南太守 label is not turned into a second hint year.

evidence.quote: 元帝之過江也，曠首創其議

itemChecks.event: The future Emperor Yuan crossed the Yangzi to Jianye.
itemChecks.reason: The hint dates his crossing, not his later 317–323 reign or a commemoration. AD 307 is the chronicle year of 始鎮建鄴 / 過江.

itemChecks.event: Zhou Yi received Wang Xizhi and offered him the ox-heart roast.
itemChecks.reason: on or before AD 322 matches claim-160 and Zhou Yi’s Yongchang 1 death. The hint is a one-sided bound, not an exact year.

itemChecks.event: Wang Dun praised Wang Xizhi as a fine youth of the clan.
itemChecks.reason: on or before AD 324 is Dun’s own speech before the Taining 2 death. No second endpoint was added.

evidence.quote: 敦嘗謂羲之曰：「汝是吾家佳子弟，當不減阮主簿。」

itemChecks.event: Ruan Yu served as Wang Dun’s clerk and was named as the measure for Xizhi.
itemChecks.reason: The hint tracks the onOrBefore AD 324 clerk-and-comparison cluster. The 王氏三少 remark stays undated and is not forced into the hint.

itemChecks.event: The empty hint is correct because Wang Cheng is only named in an undated grouping.
itemChecks.reason: s0013 lists 王承 among 王氏三少 with no year. Empty hints are required.

evidence.quote: 羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少

itemChecks.event: The empty hint is correct because Wang Yue is only named in an undated grouping.
itemChecks.reason: Same undated 三少 sentence. No active year is supported.

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian sought a Wang son-in-law, but the AD 338-339 hint treats Taiwei as a closed tenure date.
itemChecks.reason: The hint repeats the unsupported 338–339 interval. Xi Jian’s own matchmaking is real; the Western years are not a unique conversion of 時太尉. Active hints must follow a supported personal date, not a chosen title-tenure reading.

evidence.quote: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導

itemChecks.event: Xi Jian’s daughter was married to Wang Xizhi, but the AD 338-339 hint is not a unique source year.
itemChecks.reason: Her marriage (遂以女妻之) is her event, yet AD 338–339 is the same invented tenure window. The hint should not present that span as settled activity.

itemChecks.event: Yu Liang recruited Wang Xizhi as adviser and died after a deathbed memorial.
itemChecks.reason: AD 334–340 covers Liang’s own 征西 recruitment window and the AD 340 臨薨. It does not stretch his earlier court career into a dynasty-long activity band, and it does not use later commemoration.

evidence.quote: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍

personChecks.reason: Owned units give Xizhi no birth and no death. The only age is 年十三, kept as sui. His own dated acts in this slice are the Zhou Yi visit (onOrBefore 322), being praised at 亮臨薨 (AD 340), declining later court calls without a year (s0022), and, in context, the Yin Hao letters (AD 351–353). s0021 遷江州刺史 follows the memorial in narrative order and is already anchored by the 340 row; it is not a second life-date. Hints list official activity only. The east-bed marriage is narrated here but dated on p011/p012; that defect is not imported into Xizhi’s life years. No later reception is used as a living date.

evidence.quote: 亮臨薨，上疏稱羲之清貴有鑒裁

personChecks.reason: Dao’s owned row is only the undated 司徒 kinship label. Context 王丞相時 supplies the 317–339 hint for one remembered attempt to recruit Xizhi. He also appears alive in the marriage anecdote (求女婿于導). No birth or death is stated in s0001–s0022; Xiankang 5 death is external and correctly not turned into an owned death claim. No contradiction with Xizhi’s chronology.
Wang Zheng appears only as 祖正，尚書郎. No age, birth, death, or date context is omitted because none is present.
Kuang has an undated Huainan title and one dated act, 首創其議 at Yuan’s crossing (AD 307). Genealogy office and crossing counsel are kept separate. No birth or death is in these units.

The only owned event is 元帝之過江, his own crossing in Yongjia 1 / AD 307, written with the later name 元帝. Accession, reign, and death lie outside these units and are not used as activity. The hint matches that crossing only.

Zhou Yi’s only dated act here is receiving Xizhi. Yongchang 1 death supplies onOrBefore 322 and is not extracted as a death claim from a chapter that never says he died. Age 五十四 is in his own biography, not in these units.
Dun’s owned acts are esteeming Xizhi and comparing him with Ruan. Taining 2 death gives onOrBefore 324. No birth is present; his death is external terminus, not a life claim in this chapter.
Ruan Yu is Dun’s clerk, the named standard, and the speaker of 王氏三少. Only the clerk/comparison cluster has a terminus (Dun’s death, AD 324). The grouping of Cheng and Yue stays undated. Coherent.

evidence.quote: 裕亦目羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少

personChecks.reason: Wang Cheng is only a name in Ruan Yu’s undated list. No omitted birth, death, or age exists in the Chinese.

evidence.quote: 羲之與王承、王悅為王氏三少

personChecks.reason: Wang Yue is the same undated 三少 mention. Empty hints match the evidence.

Xi Jian’s owned chronology is the east-bed search dated AD 338–339 from 時太尉. Narrative sequence (messenger, report, 正此佳婿, marriage) is one episode, but the Western interval chooses the Xiankang 4–5 tenure and ignores the Shishuo 太傅 title and the Taining reconstruction. Wang Dao’s presence gives a firm onOrBefore 339, not a 338 start. Person-level chronology is therefore incoherent as stated: a closed two-year activity window is presented as if the source specified those years.

evidence.quote: 時太尉郗鑒使門生求女婿于導

personChecks.reason: The daughter’s only event is 遂以女妻之. She has no age, birth, or independent calendar. Pinning her marriage to AD 338–339 copies the faulty 太尉 conversion and creates false precision about her own wedding. Competing readings must stay open.

Yu Liang’s owned events are the 征西 recruitment (334–340 uncertainty) and 臨薨 / death (AD 340). Hints match those personal acts. No birth is given in these units; the death year comes from the Cheng-di annal for the same 薨, not from later reception. Sequence with Xizhi’s 長史 service is consistent.

evidence.quote: 征西將軍庾亮請為參軍，累遷長史

findings.problem: 時太尉郗鑒 is converted into a closed AD 338–339 westernInterval for Xi Jian’s son-in-law search and his daughter’s marriage, and the same span is written into both active hints. Xi Jian did hold 太尉 from Cheng-di Xiankang 4 V to Xiankang 5 VIII, but this chapter already uses 司徒導 as a non-dating label, Shishuo Xin yu tells the same anecdote as 郗太傅, and published reconstructions place 時 in Taining 1–2 (AD 323–324). The row therefore invents a 338 start and treats one title-reading as a specified Gregorian event window.
findings.action: Do not keep AD 338–339 as a certain interval and do not replace it with 323–324. Either mark the marriage unresolved, stating both the Taiwei-tenure reading and the anachronistic-title/Taining reading, or keep only the secure one-sided bound onOrBefore AD 339 from Xi Jian’s and Wang Dao’s Xiankang 5 deaths. Resynchronize hints-p011 and hints-p012 to that repaired chronology.
